external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the library app and self-service kiosks to borrow, renew, reserve, and return books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

external_entities.name: Desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who use the circulation page to extend loans, clear account blocks, and mark books returned.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: The interview says everyone at the desk uses the same shared login and the history cannot identify the individual or branch.

processes.name: Library app
processes.description: An app on members' phones used to borrow, renew, and reserve books by calling the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: Lending API
processes.description: The REST API through which loans are accessed and changed. It checks loan rules and is the only stated component that reads or writes the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: Exposure is disputed. Lending service note: "The lending API is internal-only." Interview transcript: "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." Authentication is unverified: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."

processes.name: Self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where a member scans their library card and books being borrowed or returned, then sends loan and return activity to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
processes.notes: The interview does not establish whether kiosks communicate directly with the loans database.

processes.name: Circulation page
processes.description: A page served by the lending API that desk staff use to extend loans, clear account blocks, and mark books returned by hand.
processes.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.

data_stores.name: Loans database
data_stores.description: The single current database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses, and full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: Priya corrected the earlier statement about two databases: "We merged those in the spring. It's one loans database now. The old reservations database is gone."

data_flows.name: use app
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to borrow, renew, or reserve books.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.

data_flows.name: update loans
data_flows.description: The library app calls the lending API with a member and book or title to renew a loan or place a reservation.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: The API authentication mechanism is unknown; Priya said she thinks it checks a token but would have to look.
data_flows.data_description: The member and book for loan changes, or a title and member for a reservation.

data_flows.name: send loans returns
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends each scanned loan and return to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.data_description: Loan and return records associated with the scanned member card and books.

data_flows.name: use page
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page to perform manual loan and account actions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account.
data_flows.notes: All desk staff use one shared login; the password is on a card taped under the desk.
data_flows.data_description: Account and loan records for manual changes.

data_flows.name: change account
data_flows.description: The circulation page sends desk-staff changes to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.

data_flows.name: read-write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes members, loans, and reservations in the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses, and borrowing history.

trust_boundaries.name: Council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data centre where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: Branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The branch network where the self-service kiosks are located and desk staff work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The source also states that desk staff work on the branch network.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database is confidential because it contains names, email addresses, home addresses, and full member borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: The interview states: "Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database."
